differences.what: The flat top now has real two-row openings, corner pinnacles, a checker band and five colonnettes dividing six upper windows.
The south bow has three basement lights, three principal transom openings and four second-storey sashes; the north loggia has paired Ionic columns and a pierced lower panel.

T-2565's loggia, compared at this view's scale (T-2577): Glessner's front and the tree in front of 1808 hide the loggia; only the top of the balcony's south pedestal shows, so this view cannot judge its carving or columns.

T-2566's granite, compared at this view's scale (T-2577): the tree's crown covers the front's checker band and courses and Glessner's roof hides the bow; the north return's courses are T-2564's item above.
Hidden rear elevations and concealed roof surfaces cannot be accepted from this front photograph.
The earlier low stone boundary replaces the generic iron fence with urns. Its exact post/rail sections remain reconstructed.

T-2564: the north return is laid in large dressed courses (about 0.46 m) with staggered joints, 5.5 m long as the course counts in the 1887-89 and 1948 views give it, where it was a smooth 2.8 m slab.
The original is monochrome; granite colour is not shown. Sepia/scan casts are not material colour.

T-2578 ruling: the stone parapet stops at the rear pinnacle. Every picture that sees that corner (1887, Taylor 2135, the 1888 Glessner plate, the c. 1888 view looking SW, the Glessner front, 1948) shows sky straight behind it, or in 1948 a darker wall about a course lower; the model drops it there.

T-2577: the cornice box under the lattice is laid in the front's dressed stone, so the crown reads as one stone mass from the wall head to the lattice, as the photographs show it; the brown band is gone in this render.
T-2578: the cowl ventilator this view shows over the return is built, at the place along the return it shows (about 0.58 of the return in both).

T-2578: the ventilator's cap stands higher over the coping in this print than in the render; this camera's residual or the cap's reconstructed set-back behind the face (T-2579's re-fitted cameras decide which). T-2713: ruled through the re-fitted camera, not this one. This camera (T-1883's fit) cannot judge the cap's height: it puts the rear pinnacle about 60 px right of and 40 px below the photograph's (x 1366, y 170 against 1307, 130), so the return's run and fall over the coping are its own. Read through T-2579's re-fitted camera on the 1888 Glessner plate, the cap's top stood 3.5 px (0.1 m) beyond the render's, so the cap now stands 1.05 m over the coping (0.95 before); there the photograph's top and the render's now agree to 1-2 px (x 1080-1082 against 1081-1084). Measured in this picture against the return's own courses under it (about 22 px a 0.46 m course here, 25 px in the render), the cap reads about 0.94 m over the coping against the render's 0.64 m before; that excess beyond the plate's is left to this camera's re-fit. T-2748: read through the re-fitted camera (4.1 px RMS). The print's cap (two dark discs, the upper x 1229-1257 at y 106-114, the lower at y 120-128, an upright stem under them at x 1245) tops out at x 1243, y 106; the render's at x 1232, y 119. Net of the camera's own 6 px at the rear pinnacle beside it, the cap stands about 7 px (0.13 m) higher over the coping than built, near this camera's error; but it also stands 11 px further right, which the rear pinnacle (1.5 px across) does not explain. Moved in the model, 0.3 m less set-back behind the return's face moves the render's cap 9 px right, and 0.3 m further back along the return 11 px right: the plate, Taylor 2135 and the 1887 view fix its place along the return, and its set-back (0.6 m) is the reconstructed coordinate, so this print reads the cowl about 0.3 m nearer the return's face than built. Left open for the build (carried on T-2751).

T-2578: the hall stack stands over the coping beside the ventilator, where this picture shows sky; the stack should stop below the coping, the cowl pipe plausibly being its flue's termination (left for T-2580). T-2712: fixed — the hall stack now stops at 16.1 m, under the return's coping, and the render shows sky over the coping beside the cowl as the picture does; the cowl's pipe rises from the stack's top.
T-2578: the ventilator's pipe reads pale beside the granite, as the print shows it (the colour itself is reconstructed: the print is monochrome).

T-2713: this view's camera (T-1883's fit, 9.1 px RMS on six front controls) places the rear pinnacle about 60 px right of and 40 px below the photograph's, so the north return reads longer and falls more steeply in the render than in the print. It needs a re-fit on the pinnacle apexes as T-2579 did for the other views before the return and the cap can be judged here; the print is faint at the apexes, which is why this run did not take it. T-2748: fixed by the re-fit. The camera is now solved level on the three pinnacle apexes the print shows, the front's north arris and its lattice rows and southmost third-storey light (pixel aspect 0.885, see the camera's solve), and the rear pinnacle's apex projects at x 1312.5, y 145 against the print's 1311, 139: 1.5 px across and 6 px down, inside the reading of a faint apex. The north return's run from the arris to the rear pinnacle and its coping's fall now lie on the print's to a few pixels over their whole length.

T-2714: the checker band's units are pitched 0.28 m along their rows (0.336 m before), with 0.07 m of ground between neighbours, as the 1888 Keith plate lays them; the rows are unchanged. Not judged here: the band's units are below this print's grain at Keith's distance.

T-2748: with this camera now holding grade (T-1883's grade reading at the south corner lands within 1 px vertically), the stoop can be compared here for the first time. In the c. 1888 print the landing's pierced balustrade reads at x 915-960, y 910-960 against the render's 950-990, 885-925, and the arch under the flight is a low round-headed opening at x 910-937, y 1012-1032 (about 27 x 20 px) against the render's 952-985, 973-1035 (about 33 x 62 px). The stoop stands about 35 px further left (east or south of where it is built) and its arch is far lower than built. Open for the build (carried on T-2751).

_how: verdict is unreviewed | differs | matches, set by whoever compared the side-by-side with the picture; each difference is {what, status: open | fixed | not shown}. A ticket whose ## Image gate names this building does not close while it is not "matches" (tools/image_gate.mjs).
